name: Pilatus PC-24
summary: Swiss light jet built for short and unpaved runways, with a large rear cargo door; operated in the US by owner-pilots and fractional provider PlaneSense.

wings: Low wing with only slight sweep and plain tips
engines: Two Williams FJ44-4A turbofans in pods high on the rear fuselage
fuselage: Large square-ish cargo door on the left rear fuselage
Sturdy trailing-link main gear for rough fields

tellTales: Large cargo door on the left side of the rear fuselage of a light twinjet
Nearly straight wing with plain tips under a T-tail
Rugged trailing-link landing gear on a business jet

confusedWith.howToTell: The PC-24 has plain wingtips and a big rear cargo door; the Phenom 300 has winglets and no cargo door.
The PC-24 is deeper and bulkier with a large cargo door; the CJ series is a slimmer tube with small windows.
The PC-24 is a twinjet; the PC-12 is a single-engine turboprop with a similar T-tail and cargo door.
